- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Make selective `core_attn` recomputation release the attention output retained by the output projection, reducing activation memory with fused attention.

In our fused-attention comparison, enabling ordinary `core_attn` checkpointing did not reduce peak activation memory. The output projection still saves the core-attention output for its weight gradient. This PR replaces ordinary checkpointing with `CheckpointWithoutOutput`: discard the attention output after projection and restore it before projection backward consumes it. The existing selective-recompute configuration remains the entry point.

Register recomputation on the projection output so that restoration precedes both projection backward and optional output-gate backward. When `mla_up_proj` recomputation is also enabled, register its hook first on the same tensor: restore Q/K/V, then recompute core attention.

Reject selective `core_attn` recomputation combined with `attn_proj` activation offloading during configuration validation, because both manage the projection-input storage. Remove the obsolete fused-attention recomputation warning and update the existing documentation to classify `core_attn` as output-discarding checkpointing.

## Issue tracking

Related to [#1886](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/1886), which reports no memory reduction with `core_attn` checkpointing and uses fused attention in its reproducer. This change improves memory savings by releasing the attention output retained for projection backward.

## Validation

### Added unit tests

- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py`: 32 parameterized GPU / Transformer Engine cases (4 attention variants × 2 sequence layouts × 2 dropout settings × 2 backends). Cover MHA, gated attention, MLA, and MLA with up-projection recomputation; packed/unpacked inputs; and FlashAttention/fused attention. Check storage discard/restoration, outputs, input/parameter gradients, and two outstanding forward graphs.
- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_transformer_config.py`: 24 added parameterized cases, comprising 12 conflict-rejection cases and 12 nonconflicting cases across `TransformerConfig` and `MLATransformerConfig`.

### End-to-end training

Separately from the committed unit tests, we ran five end-to-end DeepSeek-V2 Lite training controls.

Configuration: one node with 8 devices; 27 layers, hidden size 2048, 16 attention heads, sequence length 4096, BF16, FlashAttention, TP=1 / PP=4 / EP=2 / DP=2, microbatch size 1, global batch size 8, mock data, seed 42, and 20 training steps. All controls use the same execution environment and fusion settings. Initial parameter hashes match at every rank.

All five runs complete 20 forward/backward and optimizer steps, exit successfully, and record finite losses and gradient norms with no skipped steps.

#### Activation memory

Report the maximum of the per-rank `max_memory_allocated` measurements for training step 20.

| Recompute configuration | Step-20 max allocated memory (GiB) | Step-20 training loss |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary `core_attn` checkpoint | 54.107 | 8.733608 |
| Ordinary `core_attn`, independent repeat | 54.091 | 8.737156 |
| Discard-output `core_attn` | 53.663 | 8.736550 |
| Ordinary `core_attn` + `mla_up_proj` | 51.782 | 8.745314 |
| Discard-output `core_attn` + `mla_up_proj` | 51.338 | 8.740759 |

Switching core attention to discard-output reduces peak allocated memory by **0.444 GiB (454.6 MiB)**. With `mla_up_proj` recomputation already enabled, it saves a further **0.444 GiB (454.9 MiB)** relative to the matching ordinary-core-checkpoint control. Instrumentation also confirms that the core-attention output storage is released after projection.

#### Training numerical consistency

Compare matching iterations across all 20 steps. Gradient-norm differences below refer to the scalar norm logged by the trainer.

| Comparison | Maximum absolute loss difference | Maximum relative gradient-norm difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Independent repeat vs. ordinary `core_attn` baseline | 0.014456 | 1.937% |
| Discard-output vs. ordinary `core_attn` | 0.003868 | 0.584% |
| Discard-output vs. ordinary `core_attn`, both with `mla_up_proj` | 0.007325 | 1.118% |

For `core_attn` alone, both differences are smaller than those observed between independent baseline repeats. These measurements assess short-run training consistency over 20 steps with mock data.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] I have added proper typing to my new production method
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the full autoformatter script on my PR

+from unittest import mock

+import pytest
+import torch

+from megatron.core import tensor_parallel
+from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import (
+    get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_submodules,
+)
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed
+from megatron.core.transformer.attention import SelfAttention
+from megatron.core.transformer.enums import AttnBackend, AttnMaskType
+from megatron.core.transformer.multi_latent_attention import MLASelfAttention
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import MLATransformerConfig, TransformerConfig
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_layer import TransformerLayer
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+from tests.unit_tests.transformer.test_multi_latent_attention import make_test_packed_seq_params
+
+
+class TestCoreAttentionRecompute:
+    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+    def setup_and_teardown(self):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)
+        model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+        yield
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["mha", "gated", "mla", "mla_up_proj"])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("packed", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("dropout", [0.0, 0.1])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", [AttnBackend.flash, AttnBackend.fused])
+    def test_discard_output_and_backward(self, variant, packed, dropout, backend, monkeypatch):
+        """Discard storage and preserve gradients across two outstanding forward graphs."""
+        # These tests instantiate attention directly, without LanguageModule's backend setup.
+        monkeypatch.setenv("NVTE_FLASH_ATTN", "1" if backend == AttnBackend.flash else "0")
+        monkeypatch.setenv("NVTE_FUSED_ATTN", "1" if backend == AttnBackend.fused else "0")
+        monkeypatch.setenv("NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN", "0")
+        is_mla = variant.startswith("mla")
+
+        def build_attention(recompute):
+            options = dict(
+                num_layers=1,
+                hidden_size=128,
+                num_attention_heads=4,
+                use_cpu_initialization=True,
+                bf16=True,
+                params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                attention_dropout=dropout,
+                attention_backend=backend,
+                recompute_granularity="selective" if recompute else None,
+                recompute_modules=(
+                    ["core_attn", "mla_up_proj"] if variant == "mla_up_proj" else ["core_attn"]
+                ),
+            )
+            if is_mla:
+                config = MLATransformerConfig(
+                    **options,
+                    multi_latent_attention=True,
+                    q_lora_rank=32,
+                    kv_lora_rank=32,
+                    qk_head_dim=64,
+                    qk_pos_emb_head_dim=64,
+                    v_head_dim=64,
+                )
+                attention_cls = MLASelfAttention
+            else:
+                config = TransformerConfig(**options, attention_output_gate=variant == "gated")
+                attention_cls = SelfAttention
+            submodules = get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_submodules(
+                multi_latent_attention=is_mla
+            ).self_attention.submodules
+            return attention_cls(
+                config, submodules, layer_number=1, attn_mask_type=AttnMaskType.causal
+            ).cuda()
+
+        reference = build_attention(False)
+        candidate = build_attention(True)
+        candidate.load_state_dict(reference.state_dict())
+        shape = (32, 1 if packed else 2, 128)
+        inputs = [torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") for _ in range(2)]
+        grad_outputs = [torch.randn_like(x) for x in inputs]
+        packed_seq_params = make_test_packed_seq_params(32) if packed else None
+        saved_outputs = []
+        checkpoint = tensor_parallel.CheckpointWithoutOutput.checkpoint
+
+        def record_checkpoint(instance, *args, **kwargs):
+            result = checkpoint(instance, *args, **kwargs)
+            saved_outputs.extend(instance.outputs)
+            return result
+
+        def run(attention):
+            model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(456)
+            xs = [x.detach().clone().requires_grad_() for x in inputs]
+            outputs = []
+            for x in xs:
+                output, bias = attention(x, None, packed_seq_params=packed_seq_params)
+                outputs.append(output if bias is None else output + bias)
+            if attention is candidate:
+                assert candidate._core_attn_checkpoint is None
+                assert len(saved_outputs) == (8 if variant == "mla_up_proj" else 2)
+                assert all(t.untyped_storage().nbytes() == 0 for t in saved_outputs)
+            for output, grad in reversed(list(zip(outputs, grad_outputs))):
+                output.backward(grad)
+            return outputs, [x.grad for x in xs]
+
+        expected_outputs, expected_grads = run(reference)
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            tensor_parallel.CheckpointWithoutOutput, "checkpoint", record_checkpoint
+        ):
+            actual_outputs, actual_grads = run(candidate)
+
+        assert all(t.untyped_storage().nbytes() > 0 for t in saved_outputs)
+        for expected, actual in zip(expected_outputs, actual_outputs):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        for expected, actual in zip(expected_grads, actual_grads):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
+        for (name, expected), (actual_name, actual) in zip(
+            reference.named_parameters(), candidate.named_parameters()
+        ):
+            assert name == actual_name
+            assert (expected.grad is None) == (actual.grad is None), name
+            if expected.grad is not None:
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual.grad, expected.grad, msg=name)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("core_recompute", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("raw_output", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("packed", [False, True])

+        monkeypatch.setenv("NVTE_FUSED_ATTN", "0")
+        monkeypatch.setenv("NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN", "0")
+        modules = ["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]
+        if core_recompute:
+            modules.append("core_attn")
+
+        def build_layer(recompute):

+                num_attention_heads=8,
+                ffn_hidden_size=1024,
+                use_cpu_initialization=True,
+                bf16=True,
+                params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                attention_dropout=0.0,
+                hidden_dropout=0.0,
+                attention_backend=AttnBackend.flash,
+                normalization="RMSNorm",
+                multi_latent_attention=True,
+                q_lora_rank=None,
+                kv_lora_rank=64,
+                qk_head_dim=64,
+                qk_pos_emb_head_dim=64,
+                v_head_dim=64,
+                recompute_granularity="selective" if recompute else None,
+                recompute_modules=modules,
+            )
+            return TransformerLayer(
+                config,
+                get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_submodules(multi_latent_attention=True),
+                layer_number=1,
+            ).cuda()
+
+        reference = build_layer(False)
+        candidate = build_layer(True)
+        candidate.load_state_dict(reference.state_dict())
+        shape = (32, 1 if packed else 2, 512)
+        inputs = [torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") for _ in range(2)]
+        grad_outputs = [torch.randn_like(x) for x in inputs]
+        packed_seq_params = make_test_packed_seq_params(32) if packed else None
+        saved_outputs = []
+        norm_outputs = []
+        dependencies = {}
+        events = []
+        checkpoint = tensor_parallel.CheckpointWithoutOutput.checkpoint
+        recompute = tensor_parallel.CheckpointWithoutOutput._recompute
+
+        def record_checkpoint(instance, *args, **kwargs):
+            result = checkpoint(instance, *args, **kwargs)
+            if instance is getattr(candidate, "input_layernorm_checkpoint", None):
+                normalized = result[0] if isinstance(result, tuple) else result
+                norm_outputs.append(normalized)
+                dependencies[instance] = (len(norm_outputs) - 1, "norm")
+                saved_outputs.append(normalized)
+            elif instance is getattr(candidate.self_attention, "qkv_up_checkpoint", None):
+                dependencies[instance] = (len(norm_outputs) - 1, "up")
+                saved_outputs.extend(instance.outputs)
+            elif instance is getattr(candidate.self_attention, "_core_attn_checkpoint", None):
+                dependencies[instance] = (len(norm_outputs) - 1, "core")
+                saved_outputs.extend(instance.outputs)
+            return result
+
+        def check_recompute(instance, grad):
+            if instance.ctx is not None and instance in dependencies:
+                graph, stage = dependencies[instance]
+                if stage in ("up", "core"):
+                    assert norm_outputs[graph].untyped_storage().nbytes() > 0
+                    assert (graph, "norm") in events
+                if stage == "core":
+                    assert (graph, "up") in events
+                events.append((graph, stage))

+        def run(layer):

+
+        expected_outputs, expected_grads = run(reference)
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(
+                tensor_parallel.CheckpointWithoutOutput, "checkpoint", record_checkpoint
+            ),

+            ),
+        ):

+        assert all(t.untyped_storage().nbytes() > 0 for t in saved_outputs)
+        for graph in range(2):

+            assert [stage for index, stage in events if index == graph] == expected
+        for expected, actual in zip(expected_outputs, actual_outputs):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        for expected, actual in zip(expected_grads, actual_grads):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
+        for (name, expected), (actual_name, actual) in zip(
+            reference.named_parameters(), candidate.named_parameters()
+        ):

+            assert (expected.grad is None) == (actual.grad is None), name
+            if expected.grad is not None:
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual.grad, expected.grad, msg=name)

+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import MLATransformerConfig, TransformerConfig

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("config_cls", [TransformerConfig, MLATransformerConfig])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("recompute_modules", [None, ["core_attn"], ["core_attn", "layernorm"]])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offload_modules", [["attn_proj"], ["core_attn", "attn_proj"]])
+def test_core_attn_recompute_rejects_projection_offload(
+    config_cls, recompute_modules, offload_modules
+):
+    """Reject competing storage owners before attention modules are constructed."""
+    with pytest.raises(
+        ValueError, match="core_attn in recompute_modules cannot be combined with attn_proj"
+    ):
+        config_cls(
+            num_layers=1,
+            hidden_size=128,
+            num_attention_heads=4,
+            recompute_granularity="selective",
+            recompute_modules=recompute_modules,
+            fine_grained_activation_offloading=True,
+            offload_modules=offload_modules,
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("config_cls", [TransformerConfig, MLATransformerConfig])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "overrides",
+    [
+        pytest.param({"fine_grained_activation_offloading": False}, id="offloading-disabled"),
+        pytest.param({"recompute_granularity": None}, id="recompute-disabled"),
+        pytest.param({"recompute_modules": ["layernorm"]}, id="other-recompute-module"),
+        pytest.param({"recompute_modules": []}, id="no-recompute-modules"),
+        pytest.param({"offload_modules": ["core_attn"]}, id="other-offload-module"),
+        pytest.param(

+                "recompute_method": "uniform",
+                "recompute_num_layers": 1,
+            },

inline_comments.body:
**Restore input-layernorm output before MLA up-projection replay.**

**Failure:** Build a training `TransformerLayer` with the TE MLA submodules, `q_lora_rank=None`, and selective `recompute_modules=["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]`; run forward and backward on a gradient-enabled input. Without Q-LoRA, [`_qkv_down_projection`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L727-L746) passes the normalized hidden states directly through as `q_compressed`. That tensor becomes a saved input of the up-projection checkpoint.

This change registers up-projection replay on the projection output **before** the enclosing layer registers its [input-layernorm restoration hook](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L743-L749) on the same tensor. Hooks execute in registration order, so up-projection replay reads the still-discarded, zero-byte normalized input. Backward must instead restore that input before recomputing `linear_q_proj`. The [base implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/b67127774ca558442fb566a3df6a50862c04e4b8/megatron/core/transformer/multi_latent_attention.py#L538-L548) registered up-projection replay on the core-attention output, allowing the parent's projection-output hook to run first.

**Correction:** Make the attention/TransformerLayer hook boundary enforce `input-layernorm restoration → MLA up-projection replay → core-attention replay → projection backward`. Account for both `attention_bda_and_cross_attention` and [`_forward_self_attention_output_with_bias`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L717-L720). The exact graph-boundary implementation needs verification against CUDA-graph/offload contracts; simply reversing all hooks or restoring the old up-projection placement is not a complete fix.

**Preservation:** Keep the current Q/K/V-before-core-attention ordering when both recomputation modules are selected. Retain ordinary MLA with Q-LoRA, up-projection-only recomputation, MHA/gated attention, and the packed/unpacked cases.

**Acceptance — proposed regression checks, not executed:** Use the new test's small BF16 MLA dimensions inside a full `TransformerLayer`, but set `q_lora_rank=None`; compare `["layernorm", "mla_up_proj"]` and `["layernorm", "mla_up_proj", "core_attn"]` against identical non-recomputed models. Backward must complete, the normalized input storage must be restored before up-projection replay reads it, and outputs plus input/parameter gradients must match. Retain the [existing test's](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/091d511c133395734cbffe805191959cfbd6430a/tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_core_attention_recompute.py#L92-L124) two-outstanding-graph, zero-storage-before-backward, restored-storage-after-backward, and gradient-parity assertions.

Thanks for catching this. I confirmed that this PR introduces a hook-ordering regression with `q_lora_rank=None` and selective `layernorm` + `mla_up_proj` recomputation, both with and without `core_attn` recomputation. We will submit the fix and its regression tests in a single follow-up commit.

The fix creates a separate autograd boundary after the projection offload group commit and before MLA returns, using `make_viewless_tensor(output.view_as(output), requires_grad=output.requires_grad, keep_graph=True)`. The returned tensor shares the original output storage and remains viewless without copying the output data. The enclosing layer registers its layernorm recomputation hook on this new tensor, while the up/core hooks retain their existing order on the original projection output. This enforces **input-layernorm recomputation → MLA up-projection recomputation → core-attention recomputation → projection backward**.

We will also update the TransformerLayer regression tests to cover this recomputation combination and both call paths.
